title: Autonomous VPC Fabric Terraform Module: subnets, NAT/IGW, endpoints, routing & health checks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a production-ready Terraform module that codifies Redwood's VPC fabric for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should provision AZ-aware subnets (public, private with NAT, and isolated), attach Internet Gateway where needed, configure NAT Gateways with failover/billing-conscious options, create and manage VPC endpoints (S3, ECR, SecretsManager, KMS, STS), and provide flexible route table and routing policy primitives. It must include automated health checks and observable signals (flow logs, endpoint reachability probes), clear inputs/outputs for reuse across Private and Dedicated deployments, and a safe upgrade path for existing customer VPCs. Focus is on idempotency, minimal blast radius during upgrades, and compatibility with our private control plane PKI/KMS integrations.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes inputs for: cidr_block, az_count, subnet_sizes, nat_mode{single,per-az}, enable_flow_logs, endpoints_list, tags
Deploys public/private/isolated subnets across N AZs and outputs subnet IDs grouped by purpose
Creates either managed NAT Gateways (default) or an option to use a single shared NAT with explicit billing warning
Provision VPC endpoints: interface endpoints for ECR/SSM/SecretsManager/KMS/STS and gateway endpoint(s) for S3 with correct route table associations
Route tables and propagation are explicit; module supports custom route injection for cross-account peering and transit setups
Health checks: periodic reachability probe to each configured interface endpoint (via Lambda or local probe) and a Terraform-driven null_resource that fails deploy if endpoint unreachable in new AZ
Upgrade strategy documented: stateful resource rename plan, migration steps for switching NAT modes, and automated plan checks in CI
Automated unit/integration tests via Terratest or kitchen-terraform run in CI with a small sandbox account
Module publishes semantic version tags and CHANGELOG; breaking changes must include migration guide
Security gating: module refuses to enable public ingress on core subnets unless explicit approval flag is set
design_notes: Subnets: canonical 3-tier per AZ - public (IGW), private (NAT), isolated (no egress) to host sensitive workloads
NAT design: default per-AZ NAT Gateway for HA; optional single shared NAT with explicit cost/latency tradeoff flag 'nat_mode'
Endpoints: use interface endpoints for services requiring private DNS (ECR, SecretsManager, KMS) and gateway for S3; support endpoint policies via input map
Routing: avoid implicit route table creation; make associations explicit and allow 'extra_routes' input for overlay networks
Health checks: implement lightweight Lambda-based TCP/HTTPS probes that run on schedule and write to CloudWatch metrics and logs; Terraform provides initial synchronous check during apply
Flow logs: recommend partner integration with our observability pipeline; support enabling to S3/CloudWatch and configuring retention
State & upgrades: keep resource names stable across releases; when changing resource types, provide a 'migrate' helper script and terraform state mv guidance
IAM & KMS: module creates minimal least-privilege IAM roles for endpoint policy attachments and health-check lambdas; KMS integration must accept external key ARN input
